title: File I/O & Standard Packages
intro: File I/O in Go is built on the io.Reader and io.Writer interfaces — two of the most important interfaces in the Go standard library. This module covers os.ReadFile and os.WriteFile for simple whole-file operations, os.Open and os.Create for streaming large files (the defer f.Close() pattern — forgetting this leaks a file descriptor), bufio.Scanner for reading a file line by line without loading it all into memory, bufio.Writer for buffered writes (fewer syscalls), the io.Reader and io.Writer interfaces (what makes them powerful: any type that implements Read([]byte)(int, error) can be used as a Reader — files, network connections, in-memory buffers, HTTP response bodies all satisfy the interface), io.Copy for efficiently copying between a Reader and Writer, the filepath package for platform-independent path manipulation, and reading environment variables with os.Getenv. These I/O patterns appear in real Go services and in coding interviews.
